elements.before: Urgent Care & Freestanding ED Feasibility & Market Studies

Independent, going-concern analysis for urgent care centers and freestanding emergency departments across SBA, USDA, conventional and specialty healthcare, net-lease real-estate, and health-system and platform capital. This page is our standing read on why reimbursement and payer mix, not footfall, drive value, how credentialing and ramp forecasts fail review, and the difference between the market study, the feasibility study, and the going-concern appraisal a lender requires.
elements.after: The study an urgent care lender reads should test payer contracts, credentialing and the visit ramp before it projects coverage, because reimbursement and payer mix, not footfall, drive the value of an urgent care center or a freestanding emergency department. Feasibility Study Company prepares urgent care feasibility studies for owners, physician groups, developers and their lenders, built on a market study of the trade area's payers and visits. The industry is large, sized by IBISWorld at $43.3 billion in 2024,1 and fragmented, so a new center wins on its contracts more than its corner. It is written for SBA, USDA, conventional and specialty healthcare, net-lease and health-system lenders.
